principles.text: Not good at holding shorts; swing-trades them by covering when the selling pressure is on and looking to re-short on the rebound.
Prefers taking profits on shorts into the move rather than holding for more, accepting the trade-off that a re-entry is not guaranteed and further downside may be missed.
Short-book plan: on a strong recovery from the lows (first close above the 60-min EMA) cover about half and keep part; if the market breaks above the high of the red candle, get rid of all shorts.
On very high-volatility, small-cap names he sets a wider stop (more than 2%) but uses a much smaller size than other positions.
Checks shorter timeframes to see how a stock or index reacts to support/resistance and to read market sentiment.
No single setup or style works for every new trader: start trading, try them all, and keep what fits you; even styles you drop teach useful concepts.
Prefers to short on the next stronger, multi-day rebound in sync with the general market rather than randomly short-selling intraday.
In a divergent market, small caps not participating, declining breadth and rising new lows are not a positive sign; a trending market wants small caps to participate.
When shorting, pick the weaker names in the group.
